name: Switch Mechanism
description: A hand-operated binary state broadcaster: levers, buttons, and pull-chains. Its entire job is to hold an on/off fact and announce changes on a named channel, because in a puzzle platformer the interesting question is never the switch — it is what the switch wakes up. It therefore deliberately knows nothing about its consumers: world.door_gate subscribes to the channel, and the same switch can feed a door, a platform, and a timer without this component growing any of their logic. Anything that must be stood on or weighed down is world.pressure_plate, its floor-bound sibling; a switch that also reads weight would blur the one distinction puzzle design relies on. Visual and audio state changes are presentation's job, reached through the event.

inputs.name: channelId
inputs.description: The wire name this switch broadcasts on. Consumers match on channelId, never on proximity — a puzzle's wiring should survive the level being rearranged.

inputs.name: mechanismKind
inputs.description: lever, button, or chain. Kind is a skin plus an animation cue; it changes presentation, not behavior — behavior comes from mode.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: toggle flips state on each use; momentary is on only while held or for pulseSeconds after a press. Momentary switches create timed-runs; toggles create permanent world changes.

inputs.name: initialState
inputs.description: State when the level loads, before any interaction.

inputs.name: interactRange
inputs.description: How close the player must be to use the switch. Generous ranges forgive imprecise landing; tight ones make the switch itself a platforming target.

outputs.name: state
outputs.description: The one fact this component owns. Everything downstream is someone else's reaction to it.
